purpose: Gate-fee revenue of energy-from-waste (model carrier waste_to_energy), expressed per MWh of electricity exported, for the 2040 public-ownership finance layer. The gate fee is paid by waste producers (mainly local authorities), not by electricity consumers.

gate_fee_gbp_per_tonne.basis: UK median and range for residual waste excluding bulky waste containing POPs sent to EfW, 29 local-authority responses after outlier removal. The other residual category (mixed with bulky waste containing POPs, 40 responses) has the same median, 121, mean 126, range 69 to 208.

gate_fee_price_year: 2024/25 nominal (WRAP survey fieldwork December 2024 to January 2025, fees in force in 2024/25); treated as 2024 money

gate_fee_source.title: WRAP, Gate Fees Report 2024/25 (v2)
gate_fee_source.table: Table 23: UK EfW gate fees according to material reprocessed (GBP/tonne); survey dates in section 2.0

gate_fee_cross_check_latest_edition.title: WRAP, Gate Fees Report 2025/26 (v1.0, July 2026)
gate_fee_cross_check_latest_edition.note: Not used as the central value because it is in 2025/26 money; the 2024/25 edition needs no rebasing to 2024.

mwh_exported_per_tonne.source: Tolvik Consulting, UK Energy from Waste Statistics 2024 (April 2025), section 3 Energy, Figure 5: average power export 600 kWh per tonne of input in 2024 (10,040 GWh exported from 16.82 Mt processed); 2020 to 2024 series 553, 591, 620, 605, 600 kWh/t gives the range. https://static1.squarespace.com/static/5eabdfbe067c0b62fc7b58b7/t/6800cd36c2408b1f7ad8f645/1744883006223/uk-energy-from-waste-statistics-2024-4812.pdf (accessed 2026-10-03)
mwh_exported_per_tonne.efficiency_derivation: 9.62 MJ/kg = 2.672 MWh(th)/t; 0.600 / 2.672 = 22.5% net export efficiency; gross generation 11,870 GWh / 16.82 Mt = 0.706 MWh/t (26.4%). Parasitic load 15.4% excluding imports (Tolvik Figure 5).
mwh_exported_per_tonne.electricity_only_caveat: Tolvik's fleet average includes CHP plants (1,949 GWh(th) of heat exported in 2024 beside 10,040 GWh of power, about 16% of exported energy); electricity-only plants export slightly more per tonne, so the central value is mildly conservative for gate fee per MWh.

cpi_to_2024_factor_source: No rebasing: WRAP 2024/25 gate fees were collected December 2024 to January 2025 (WRAP Gate Fees Report 2024/25, section 2.0). The bill layer treats FY2024/25 nominal values as 2024 money (data/market/neso_balancing_costs/bsuos_constraint_split_2024_25.json, price_basis_note); the same convention is applied here.

projection_2040.rule: Held flat in real terms (2024 money). No source found giving a real-terms gate-fee projection to 2040.
projection_2040.fes_context: FES 2025 Holistic Transition 2040: waste_to_energy 3,422 MW, 10,951 GWh (resources/FES/fes2025_holistic_transition_2040_targets.csv, ES1). At 0.600 MWh/t that is about 18.3 Mt of waste a year; at 121 GBP/t about GBP 2.21 bn of gate-fee revenue in 2040.
projection_2040.upside_risk: Gate fees rose 6.6% nominal between the 2024/25 and 2025/26 editions (121 to 129 for residual waste excluding bulky POPs). WRAP 2025/26 interviewees cite the potential inclusion of EfW plants in the UK Emissions Trading Scheme as a source of future cost uncertainty; Tolvik reports about 1.00 t CO2 per tonne of residual waste input (biogenic plus fossil). A carbon cost passed through to gate fees would raise the per-MWh figure; not included in the central value.

notes: Gate fee is revenue to the EfW operator for waste disposal, separate from electricity market revenue; it should reduce the electricity price the asset needs, not be added to any consumer electricity bill line.
Medians are of local-authority-reported contract fees; merchant commercial and industrial waste fees can differ.
Units: GBP per tonne of waste input; GBP per MWh of net electricity exported.
derived_from: data/public_ownership/financing/efw_gate_fees_2050.json (11 Nov 2026): every value year-neutral (2024 money), only the FES context moved to 2040
